x: The Delhi Sultanate dynasties ran Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughluq (1320), Sayyid (1414) and Lodi (1451). Leaving out the Tughluqs, the order is B, D, C, A.

t: Match each dynasty with its capital.

x: Nanyadev founded the Karnata dynasty of Mithila. Nannuka founded the Chandelas, Vijayalaya the imperial Cholas and Anangpal Tomar is linked with the Tomars.

x: Nannuka founded the Chandela, Anangpal Tomar the Tomar, Nanyadev the Karnata and Gopala the Pala dynasty, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

x: The Nizamshahis ruled from Ahmednagar, the Adilshahis from Bijapur, the Imadshahis from Berar and the Baridshahis from Bidar, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

x: Harihara I and Bukka I began the Sangama line, Narasimha Saluva the Saluva, Vira Narasimha the Tuluva, and Tirumala Deva Raya, brother of Aliya Rama Raya, founded the Aravidu dynasty after Talikota, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

Match List-I with List-II.

x: All three are correct: Vijayanagara was ruled in turn by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties; Narasimha Saluva began the Saluva line and Vira Narasimha the Tuluva line.

x: I, II and IV are correct: Mayurasharman founded the Kadambas, Nannuka the Chandelas and Vijayalaya revived Chola power in the 9th century. III is false because Kharavela was the greatest ruler of the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) dynasty of Kalinga, not its founder.
t: Discriminate the founder of a dynasty from its most famous ruler.

x: Both are true: Bundelkhand was called Jejakabhukti after the Chandela ruler Jayashakti or Jeja, and Anangpal Tomar is credited with founding Dhillika, the early Delhi.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Vijayanagara was ruled by the Sangama (from 1336), Saluva (from 1485), Tuluva (from 1505) and Aravidu (from 1570) dynasties, giving C, D, A, B.
t: Arrange the Vijayanagara dynasties by their starting years.

x: Three are correct: Vasudeva Kanva–Kanva, Mayurasharman–Kadamba and Nannuka–Chandela. Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur dynasty; the Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala.
t: Check each founder–dynasty pair separately.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Vindhyashakti began the Vakataka line, but Pravarasena I built it into a large kingdom and alone took the title Samrat, so he is called its real founder.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.
s:
Assertion (A): Pravarasena I is regarded as the real founder of the Vakataka dynasty.
Reason (R): Pravarasena I expanded the Vakataka kingdom and was the only Vakataka ruler to take the title Samrat.

x: Nagabhata I founded the Gurjara-Pratihara line and checked the Arabs, Vatsaraja opened the Tripartite Struggle with the Palas and Rashtrakutas, Siyaka II is the real founder of the Paramaras and Samantasena founded the Senas, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Discriminate the founder from the real or actual founder.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Nagabhata I
(b) Vatsaraja
(c) Siyaka II
(d) Samantasena

i. Real founder of the Paramara dynasty
ii. Founder of the Sena dynasty

x: Both are true: Golconda was the capital of the Qutbshahis, and Amir Ali Barid founded the Baridshahi dynasty of Bidar.

t: Check each statement separately.

x: Option D is correct: Jayashakti (Jeja) was the grandson of the Chandela founder Nannuka, and Jejakabhukti was named after him. The other options wrongly bring in Nanyadev or Anangpal Tomar.
t: Link Jejakabhukti to the Chandela line.

x: Harihara I and Bukka I, the Sangama brothers, founded Vijayanagara in 1336. Nagabhata I and Vatsaraja were Pratiharas; the other pairs founded Bahmani successor states.
t: Match each pair of rulers with their kingdom.

x: Pulakesin I founded the Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi) in the 6th century. Vijayalaya founded the imperial Cholas, Nanyadev the Karnata dynasty and Mayurasharman the Kadambas.
t: Match each founder with his dynasty.

x: Shrisantamula founded the Ikshvakus, Mayurasharman the Kadambas, Kharavela was the great Chedi ruler of Kalinga and Nannuka founded the Chandelas, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Link each ruler to his dynasty.

x: Both are true: Fatehullah Imad Shah founded the Imadshahi dynasty of Berar, and Babur established Mughal rule in India in 1526.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar records the reign of Kharavela, the Chedi king of Kalinga, year by year.
t: Link the inscription to the ruler it describes.

x: Samantasena founded the Sena dynasty of Bengal. Vatsaraja was a Pratihara, Nanyadev founded the Karnata dynasty and Gopala the Palas.
t: Match each founder with his dynasty.

x: Malik Sarwar, a Tughluq noble titled Malik-us-Sharq, founded the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur. The Lodi, Sayyid and Tughluq dynasties had other founders.

x: Both are true: Jayashakti, or Jeja, was the grandson of the Chandela founder Nannuka, and the Kanva dynasty succeeded the Shungas.

x: The Mauryan Empire lasted from about 322 to 185 BCE, so it falls in the 4th–2nd century BCE. The other options are CE periods of later dynasties.

x: The Vesara style, a mix of Nagara and Dravida temple forms, is linked with the Chalukyas of Badami, seen at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Rashtrakutas ruled from the 8th to the 10th century CE, ending in 973. The Rashtrakuta 8th–10th, Pratihara 8th–11th and Pala 8th–12th periods are right.

x: Rajendra Chola belongs to the Cholas, Raja Bhoj to the Paramaras, Khajuraho to the Chandelas and Hampi to Vijayanagara, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

x: The Bahmani kingdom ran from the 14th to the 16th century, the Mughals from the 16th to the 18th, the Marathas from the 17th century onward and the Sikh Empire in the 19th, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

x: Hampi was the Vijayanagara capital, the Bahmanis ruled the Deccan, Akbar and Aurangzeb were Mughals and Shivaji founded the Maratha state, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.

x: All three are correct: Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka were Mauryas, the Gupta age is called the Golden Age, and Mamallapuram's monuments were built by the Pallavas.

x: I and II are correct: Vijayanagara lasted from the 14th to the 17th century and the Bahmanis from the 14th to the 16th. III is false because the Mughal period was the 16th–18th century, from 1526.
t: Recall the century span of each empire.

x: Both are true: the Palas of Bengal were great patrons of Buddhism, founding Vikramashila, and the Pratiharas were a major North Indian power ruling from Kannauj.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Guptas began in the 4th century CE, the Pallavas rose in the 6th, the Rashtrakutas in the 8th and the imperial Cholas in the 9th, giving A, B, D, C.
t: Arrange the dynasties by the century they began.

x: All four are persons: Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka for the Mauryas, Rajendra Chola for the Cholas, Raja Bhoj for the Paramaras and Ranjit Singh for the Sikh Empire.

x: The Chalukyas of Badami ruled from the 6th to the 8th century CE, from about 543 until the Rashtrakutas replaced them in 753.

x: The Kanva dynasty succeeded the Shungas when Vasudeva Kanva overthrew Devabhuti, the last Shunga king. The Mauryas came before the Shungas.

x: The Shungas followed the Mauryas, the Kanvas the Shungas, the Khaljis the Slave dynasty and the Tughlaqs the Khaljis, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.

x: Both are true: the Sayyid dynasty succeeded the Tughlaqs, and Khizr Khan began it when he took Delhi in 1414.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Narasimha Saluva ended Sangama rule, Vira Narasimha began Tuluva rule, Tirumala Deva Raya began Aravidu rule after Talikota, and Pushyamitra Shunga replaced the Mauryas, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.

x: Both are true: the Tuluva dynasty followed the Saluvas, and Vira Narasimha began Tuluva rule in 1505.

x: All three are correct: Vijayanagara was ruled in turn by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties.

x: Vira Narasimha of the Tuluva family took the throne from Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva king, in 1505 and began Tuluva rule.

x: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan in 1211 and is seen as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate. Chhatrapati was Shivaji's title, and Kshatriya status was declared for Shivaji.

Assertion (A): Turkish nobles supported and approved Iltutmish’s succession.
Reason (R): The Turkish nobles of Delhi considered Aram Shah, Aibak's successor, incompetent.

x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, after Humayun's death. The 1658 and 1659 dates are Aurangzeb's two coronations.

x: Aurangzeb's second, formal coronation was on June 5, 1659. July 21, 1658 was his first, and February 14, 1556 was Akbar's enthronement.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: June 5, 1659 only dates the second coronation; the reason it came then was his victories over Shuja at Khajwa and Dara at Deorai.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: after Rajaram died in 1700, Tarabai placed her four-year-old son on the throne, and he ruled as Shivaji II.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Option C is incorrect: Chandragupta II was called Sakari, the Saka-conqueror; Satyashraya was a title of Pulakeshin II. Ashoka as Devanampiya, Harsha as Shiladitya and Kushana Devaputra are right.

x: Rajaraja I was called Mummudi Chola, Shah Jahan was earlier Prince Khurram, Ranjit Singh was the Lion of Punjab and J. B. Kripalani was known as Acharya, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

x: Three are correct: Chandragupta II–Sakari, Alauddin Khalji–Sikandar-i-Sani and Bairam Khan–Khan-i-Khanan. Pair IV is wrong: Sikandar-i-Sani was Alauddin Khalji's title, not Shankaracharya's.
t: Check each title–person pair separately.

x: Chandragupta I took Maharajadhiraja, the Kushanas used Devaputra, Rajaraja I was Mummudi Chola, the three-crowned Chola, and Aybak was Sipahsalar, the commander, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

x: All four are correct: Chandragupta II was Vikramaditya and was also called Devagupta, Devashri and Devaraja in inscriptions, which are his Deva titles.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Padshah
 b. Ghazi
 c. Zinda Pir

List-II
 i. Babur, at Kabul in 1507

x: Shah Jahan means King of the World, a title Prince Khurram took on his accession. Alamgir means Conqueror of the World, Sakari Saka-conqueror and Devanampiya Beloved of the Gods.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Alamgir means Conqueror of the World from its Persian roots, not because Aurangzeb used it as his title.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Param Bhagavata, devoted follower of Vishnu, shows Vaishnavite faith and was used by the Gupta rulers, including Samudragupta. Devaputra was Kushana, Maharajadhiraja an imperial title and Satyashraya Chalukya.
t: Link the title to its religious meaning.

x: I and II are correct: Satyashraya was a Chalukya title held by Pulakeshin II. III is false because Gangaikonda Chola was the title of Rajendra I, the Chola king.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Aybak was called Sipahsalar, Alauddin Khalji styled himself Sikandar-i-Sani, the second Alexander, Balban was Zil-i-Ilahi and Rajendra I was Gangaikonda Chola, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall each ruler's distinctive title and match it once.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Qutbuddin Aybak
 b. Alauddin Khalji
 c. Balban
 d. Rajendra I

List-II
 i. Zil-i-Ilahi
 ii. Gangaikonda Chola
 iii. Sipahasalaar
 iv. Sikandar-i-Sani

x: Two are correct: Aybak was called Sipahsalar and Quran Khwan. Zil-i-Ilahi was Balban's title and Gangaikonda Chola was Rajendra I's.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Zil-i-Ilahi means Shadow of God, a title Balban used for divine kingship. God's representative is Niyabat-i-Khudai, his other title, and Second Alexander is Alauddin's Sikandar-i-Sani.
t: Discriminate Zil-i-Ilahi from Niyabat-i-Khudai.

x: A is true: Farid Khan got the title Sher Khan for killing a tiger. B is false because Akbar gave Bairam Khan the title Khan-i-Khanan, not Sher Khan.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Aurangzeb was called Zinda Pir, the living saint, for his simple and pious life. Chandragupta II was Vikramaditya and Samudragupta the Napoleon of India.
t: Match each epithet with its ruler.

x: Option C is incorrect: Saadat Khan of Awadh was titled Burhan-ul-Mulk; Sarvalokeshvara was the title of the Kushana king Vima Kadphises. Chin Qilich Khan as Nizam-ul-Mulk and Asaf Jah is right.
t: Match each title with its ruler.

x: Option C is incorrect: Vima Kadphises was called Sarvalokeshvara; Vikramaditya was Chandragupta II. Asaf Jah for Chin Qilich Khan, Mubarak Khalji and Samudragupta as Napoleon of India are right.
t: Match each title with its ruler.

x: Option C is incorrectly matched: Asaf Jah was the title of Chin Qilich Khan, the Nizam-ul-Mulk of Hyderabad. Mubarak Shah Khalji called himself Al-Imam and Khalifatullah.
t: Match each title with its ruler.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Kadphises II is only his regnal number; the title Sarvalokeshvara, lord of all the world, came from his Shaivite devotion and power.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: I, II and III are correct: Samudragupta was the Napoleon of India, Chandragupta II Vikramaditya and Aurangzeb Zinda Pir. IV is false because Ghazi Malik was Ghiyasuddin Tughluq; Vima Kadphises was Sarvalokeshvara.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Samudragupta was the Napoleon of India, Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, Vima Kadphises Sarvalokeshvara and Aurangzeb Zinda Pir, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each epithet with its ruler.

x: Ghiyasuddin Tughluq was Ghazi Malik, Mubarak Shah Khalji Al-Imam, Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk and Chin Qilich Khan Nizam-ul-Mulk, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each title with its ruler.

x: Vima Kadphises was Sarvalokeshvara, Ghiyasuddin was Ghazi Tughluq, Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk and Chin Qilich Khan Asaf Jah, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each title with its ruler.

x: Three are correct: Samudragupta–Napoleon of India, Chandragupta II–Vikramaditya and Saadat Khan–Burhan-ul-Mulk. Pair IV is wrong: Sarvalokeshvara was Vima Kadphises; Chin Qilich Khan was Nizam-ul-Mulk.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty, who expanded Magadha by marriage and conquest of Anga, was a contemporary and follower of the Buddha in the 6th century BCE.
t: Link the early Magadhan kings to the Buddha's lifetime.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Ajatashatru is linked with the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha (about 483 BCE) because he was its royal patron.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: I, II and III are correct: Ashoka spread Dhamma through his inscriptions and built stupas to spread Buddhism. IV is false because Mauryan power was extended into the Deccan by Bindusara.
t: Discriminate Ashoka's work from Bindusara's.

x: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire with a central administration, Bindusara pushed into the Deccan, Kanishka patronised Mahayana Buddhism with Nagarjuna, and Samudragupta's conquests are in the Prayaga Prashasti, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Link each ruler to his main achievement.

x: Chandragupta II, called Vikramaditya, marked Gupta cultural growth, Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda, Skandagupta resisted the Hunas, and Harsha patronised Banabhatta and wrote the play Nagananda, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Link each ruler to his main achievement.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Chandragupta II
(b) Kumaragupta I
(c) Skandagupta
(d) Harshavardhana

List-II
(i) Resistance against Hunas
(ii) Patron of Banabhatta; author of Nagananda
(iii) Gupta cultural expansion; Vikramaditya
(iv) Founder of Nalanda Mahavihara

x: Both are true: Samudragupta ruled about 335–375 CE, and his son Chandragupta II ruled about 375–415 CE.
t: Recall the reign years of the Gupta kings.

x: Karikala Chola of the Sangam age built the Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across the Kaveri for irrigation. Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulottunga I were later imperial Cholas.
t: Discriminate the Sangam Cholas from the imperial Cholas.

x: Rajendra I led the Ganga expedition and naval campaigns, Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara Temple, Kulottunga I strengthened administration and overseas trade, and Narasimhavarman I built at Mamallapuram, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each ruler to his main achievement.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Mahendravarman I began Pallava rock-cut cave temples; his son Narasimhavarman I's later Mamallapuram work cannot explain his father's role.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Vijayanagara reached its political and cultural peak under Krishnadeva Raya (1509–1529), a great general and the patron of the Ashtadiggajas.
t: Recall the greatest ruler of Vijayanagara.

x: Aibak founded the Slave dynasty and began the Qutub Minar, Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate, issued the tanka and jital and completed the Minar, Balban built a strong monarchy, and Alauddin made market and military reforms, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Link each Sultan to his main achievement.

x: Option C is incorrect: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504, not Delhi. Razia as the only woman Sultan, Firoz Shah's canals and Muhammad bin Tughluq's token currency are right.
t: Recall the city Sikandar Lodi founded.

x: Both are true: Muhammad bin Tughluq ruled from 1325 to 1351, and his cousin Firoz Shah Tughluq from 1351 to 1388.
t: Recall the reign years of the Tughluq Sultans.

x: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and wrote his memoir, the Baburnama, in Turki. Humayun, Akbar and Jahangir came after him.
t: Recall the founder of the Mughal Empire.

x: Humayun laid the foundation of Mughal painting, Akbar expanded the empire with reforms, Jahangir's reign was the peak of painting and Shah Jahan's the peak of architecture, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Link each Mughal emperor to his main achievement.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri was a law digest; the empire's greatest extent came from his Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Shivaji founded the Maratha state with the Ashtapradhan, Sambhaji kept up resistance to the Mughals, Balaji Vishwanath built up Peshwa power and Baji Rao I expanded into North India, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Link each Maratha leader to his main achievement.

x: All four are correct: Shivaji lived in the 17th century, Sambhaji ruled 1680–1689, Balaji Vishwanath was Peshwa 1713–1720 and Baji Rao I 1720–1740.
t: Check each ruler's years separately.

x: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled 1236–1240 and was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Chand Bibi, Nur Jahan and Durgavati were not Sultans of Delhi.
t: Recall the only woman ruler of Delhi.

x: Bimbisara belongs to the 6th century BCE, Ajatashatru to the 6th–5th century BCE, Ashoka ruled c. 268–232 BCE and Kanishka in the 2nd century CE, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the period of each ruler.

x: Karikala Chola belongs to the Sangam age, Narasimhavarman I to the 7th century, Rajendra Chola I to the 11th and Krishnadeva Raya to 1509–1529, giving A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the rulers by century.

x: Both are true: Humayun ruled 1530–1540, lost the throne to Sher Shah, and ruled again 1555–1556; Jahangir ruled 1605–1627.
t: Recall the reign years of the Mughal emperors.

x: Two are linked with Muhammad bin Tughluq: token currency and moving the capital to Daulatabad. Strong monarchy belongs to Balban and the founding of Agra to Sikandar Lodi.
t: Check each item against the ruler.

x: Babur ruled 1526–1530, Akbar 1556–1605, Shah Jahan 1628–1658 and Aurangzeb 1658–1707, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the reign years of the Mughal emperors.

x: Both are true: Chandragupta Maurya ruled about 321–297 BCE, and his son Bindusara about 297–273 BCE.
t: Recall the reign years of the early Mauryas.

x: Chandragupta II ruled c. 375–415 CE, Kumaragupta I c. 415–455, Skandagupta c. 455–467 and Harshavardhana c. 606–647, giving A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the rulers by reign years.

x: All four are correct: Rajaraja I ruled 985–1014 CE, Kulottunga I belongs to the 11th–12th century, and the Pallavas Mahendravarman I and his son Narasimhavarman I both ruled in the 7th century.
t: Check each ruler's period separately.

x: Aibak ruled 1206–1210, Iltutmish 1211–1236, Balban 1266–1287 and Alauddin Khalji 1296–1316, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the reign years of the Sultans.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Aibak built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi; Iltutmish completing the Qutub Minar is a separate, later work.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Sikandar Lodi ruled 1489–1517. 1296–1316 is Alauddin Khalji, 1351–1388 Firoz Shah Tughluq and 1266–1287 Balban.
t: Match each period with its Sultan.
